lines.trans: All these people around are ungrateful scumbags.
Chef, one should not think so badly about everyone.
I taught them to cook the city's best dishes.
Every cook remembers your great lesson.
Then why are they following someone else's orders now?
They are simply afraid of losing their job.
A true master is never afraid of difficulties.
You are the main culinary master for us.
Let them handle the complex banquet themselves now.
Without your participation, chaos will break out in the kitchen.
That is great, let them see my strength!
I will stay by your side anyway.

meanings.note: a large formal meal for many people

examples.text: У нас сегодня очень важный банкет.
examples.trans: We have a very important banquet today.
A lavish banquet was hosted in the restaurant.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'without' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be afraid'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('great').
Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian preposition meaning 'around' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: She was running after me (around me).
She circled around me like a shark.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'main' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('the main thing') (neuter главное, used as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'town, city' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to prepare') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'every', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'team; command' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('command, order') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Теперь мы одна команда.
examples.trans: Nothing serious. Now we're one team.

meanings.note: connected with cooking or the kitchen

examples.text: Я отличный повар и закончил кулинарный колледж.
examples.trans: I am an excellent cook and finished culinary college.

examples.text: Ладно, сейчас проверим твои настоящие кулинарные навыки.
examples.trans: Fine, now we will test your real culinary skills.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Secondary conversational sense ('better') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'technician', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: Они совсем не похожи на настоящих мастеров.
examples.trans: They look nothing like real technicians.

examples.text: А какие признаки должны быть у мастеров?
examples.trans: And what signs should technicians have?

meanings.note: in 'рабочее место' = workplace, job
Secondary conversational sense ('post, position') (на его место = in his place) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Secondary conversational sense ('present, current') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

наступить.gloss: to come (of time); to step on

meanings.en: to come, to set in (night, winter, a moment)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ступить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come', forming an aspectual pair with 'наступать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to step on') (наступить на + accusative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: + accusative of person, + dative / infinitive

examples.trans: He taught me how to swim.

examples.text: Ура, работает приёмчик! Это меня губернатор научил.
examples.trans: Hooray, the little trick works! The governor taught me this.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'благодарный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ungrateful').

examples.text: Послушай, не клади трубку! Ах ты, неблагодарная!
examples.trans: Listen, don't hang up! Oh, you ungrateful girl!

нельзя.gloss: it is not allowed; one can't

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'it is not allowed'.
Secondary conversational sense ('impossible, can't') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

meanings.note: used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

examples.text: Я никогда в жизни не пробовал такой вкусной утки!
examples.trans: I have never in my life tasted such delicious duck!

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('they') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left
Secondary conversational sense ('to stay') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'excellently'.
Secondary conversational sense ('great!, excellent!') (as a one-word reply) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I know this town really well!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'badly'.
Secondary conversational sense ('it's bad') (predicative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'scumbag'.

examples.text: Шеф кричал, что вокруг одни подонки.
examples.trans: The chef shouted that there were only scumbags around.

examples.text: Все эти люди вокруг — неблагодарные подонки.
examples.trans: All these people around are ungrateful scumbags.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мнить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to remember'.

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to lose', paired with 'терять'.

examples.text: Что смотрите, бандерлоги? Вы совсем страх потеряли?
examples.trans: What are you staring at, you monkeys? Have you lost all fear?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'working', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('worker') (as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'next to'.
Secondary conversational sense ('nearby, close by') (adverb of place) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: A plot next to Grigory Soprykin.
Right nearby, round the corner, there's a cheburek café.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: colloquial plural силы = engine horsepower
colloquial plural силы = engine horsepower

examples.trans: How much power does this car have?

examples.text: Да, по-моему, здорово! Сколько сил в этой машине?
examples.trans: Yes, I think it's great! How much power does this car have?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ложный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('complicated, difficult').

examples.trans: Danila, let's go. Look, there's nothing complicated.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to listen', forming an aspectual pair with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'
Secondary conversational sense ('hello (on the phone)') ('Слушаю' = I'm listening) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'правляться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to cope'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Ты отлично справляешься сегодня на смене.
examples.trans: You are doing great on the shift today.

examples.text: Он легко справлялся с любой задачей.
examples.trans: He easily coped with any task.
Do not argue, Fedya managed somehow!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'difficulty, hardship' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Some people easily cope with difficulties.

examples.text: Настоящий мастер никогда не боится трудностей.
examples.trans: A true master is never afraid of difficulties.

meanings.en: to see, to catch sight of
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to see', forming an aspectual pair with 'видеть'.

examples.text: И Нину свою ты больше не увидишь!
examples.trans: And you'll never see your Nina again!

meanings.note: in уроки учить / делать уроки, plural
in уроки учить / делать уроки, plural

examples.trans: Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'participation', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: От вас я по-прежнему жду участия.
examples.trans: I still expect participation from you.

examples.text: Спасибо за ваше участие в проекте.
examples.trans: Thank you for your participation in the project.

examples.text: От вас я по-прежнему жду участия. Всё.
examples.trans: I still expect participation from you. That is all.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'chaos, disarray' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Но на кухне всегда царит полный хаос.
examples.trans: But total chaos always reigns in the kitchen.

examples.text: Без вашего участия на кухне наступит хаос.
examples.trans: Without your participation, chaos will break out in the kitchen.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Secondary conversational sense ('people') (plural люди, a different word) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: neuter чужое as a noun = other people's things
Secondary conversational sense ('stranger's, foreign') (чужой человек = a stranger) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking?

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса, да?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking, yes?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
